brief: Add all required installments and fees, distinguish total repayment from borrowing cost, and compare the same received amount and term.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Count the full repayment"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Cuenta el pago completo"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Conte o pagamento completo"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Add all required installments and fees, distinguish total repayment from borrowing cost, and compare the same received amount and term.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: A small installment can hide many payments. Count the complete obligation before comparing financing offers.
instruction.misconception: Using the smallest installment as proof of the cheapest loan while ignoring the number of payments or mandatory fees.
instruction.numeracy_support: Repeated addition computes total installments; subtract received principal to obtain borrowing cost in fully specified examples.

evidence.reasoning: A fictional loan gives 100 now and requires four payments of 30. Repayment totals 30 + 30 + 30 + 30 = 120.
With no fees, repaying 120 after receiving 100 means a cost of 20. Full repayment includes the borrowed amount.
The total includes every required installment.
Borrowing cost is the extra amount above what was received.
The number of installments changes the total comparison.
A separately required fee is part of the complete payment obligation.
Cost and ability to pay on the required dates are different checks.
Extra cost is the financed total minus the cash price.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Apply this skill in a later integrated decision with a different constraint.
